previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with severe abdominal pain, distention, and constipation three days after discharge from a prior admission for cast nephropathy in the setting of relapsed multiple myeloma. Initial evaluation revealed moderate fecal load and improving renal function with a creatinine of 2.1. He developed worsening abdominal distention and pain with guarding, leading to ICU transfer and NG tube placement for decompression due to partial bowel obstruction. Imaging confirmed duodenitis and a perivesicular mass likely representing extramedullary hematopoiesis. He experienced hypoglycemia attributed to insulin stacking and CKD, managed with D10W and insulin regimen adjustment. After stabilization, he received a four-day course of dexamethasone and Cytoxan for relapsed myeloma, underwent EGD and colonoscopy showing non-specific duodenitis and no malignancy, and completed a vancomycin taper for C. diff. His symptoms resolved, renal function improved to a creatinine of 1.5, and he was discharged home on insulin, PPI, and scheduled follow-ups with oncology, urology, and GI.
